rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 6 compounds if possible and map the overall retention window without risking severe truncation. This gives a strong first read on whether peaks are compressed early, spread across the gradient, or still retained into the high-organic hold.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is reducing t_last. The observed elution window corresponds roughly to phi_e about 0.18 to 0.36, so a narrower, shorter gradient centered on that range should keep all peaks in-gradient while cutting the run substantially.

Resolution margin is still very large, so push for a faster method by shortening the gradient and raising temperature one step. This should reduce retention enough to test whether all peaks can be brought to about 10 minutes or less while likely preserving full resolution.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now probe the speed limit by shortening tG one more step while keeping the same window and temperature. The goal is to find whether resolution remains fully acceptable at an even faster method or where the first pair starts to fail.

The current worst pair still has margin above 1.5, so take one more step shorter to locate the minimum viable gradient time. If pair 1-2 drops below full credit, we can back off to 4 minutes knowing injection 4 is the fastest fully robust setting tested so far.

With tG = 2 min the limiting pair 1-2 lost resolution, so stay at 4 min but tighten the gradient window toward the actual elution range to see if we can keep full resolution while preserving a short run. Shifting phi0 upward and phi1 slightly downward should reduce empty gradient space and may further optimize speed without over-compressing the critical early pair.

Injection 4 is the fastest fully resolved method so far; now test whether a modest temperature increase can shorten it further while keeping the limiting 1-2 pair above 1.5. This is a direct speed optimization around the current best practical method.

At 55 C the critical 1-2 pair is just under full credit, so lower phi0 one step to retain and spread the earliest peaks while keeping the run otherwise fast. This targets the only failing pair directly with minimal impact on the rest of the chromatogram.

Now test whether the same lower phi0 can preserve full resolution at the minimum gradient time of 2 minutes. This directly probes whether we can beat the 4-minute method while holding the formerly critical 1-2 pair at or above 1.5.

The 55 C, 4 min method is very close to the resolution limit only for pair 1-2, so lower phi0 one more step to give the earliest pair a bit more retention and margin. This may preserve full resolution while keeping the same short runtime regime.

Injection 8 achieved full score at 55 C with only a narrow margin on pair 1-2, so now trim phi1 one step to reduce late hold strength while keeping the successful low-phi0 condition. This tests whether we can maintain full resolution and possibly refine the method window around the actual elution range.

Since lowering phi1 made the last peak later, try the opposite direction: raise phi1 one step from the successful injection 8 to see whether the late compound can be pulled earlier without sacrificing the critical early-pair resolution. This explores whether a slightly wider, stronger gradient can give an equally perfect but faster method.

The 55 C, 4 min method is excellent but only barely fully resolving pair 1-2, so lengthen tG to 6 min at the same temperature and window to create a more robust high-temperature method. This checks whether we can keep full CRF with extra selectivity margin while still remaining under the 10-minute penalty threshold.

We have several perfect methods already, so use remaining budget to test the upper temperature limit with the successful fast window. This will show whether extra temperature can produce an even shorter viable method or confirm that 55 C is already beyond the optimum for the critical first pair.

At this point the optimization is around the resolution cliff for pair 1-2, so test a slightly narrower window shifted upward from injection 8/11 to map that boundary more completely. Comparing this with the successful 0.10/0.60 and 0.10/0.55 runs will clarify whether the best 55 C fast method is uniquely centered near phi0 0.10.

A slightly higher-start, narrower window at 55 C still gave full resolution, so now raise phi1 one step to see if the last peak can be accelerated without pushing the 1-2 pair below 1.5. This is a focused attempt to find a faster perfect method than the existing 55 C options.

We have mapped several successful 55 C windows around phi0 0.10–0.15, so test a higher phi0 with the standard phi1 to complete the boundary on the critical early pair. This should confirm whether increasing the start strength consistently pushes pair 1-2 toward failure while possibly shortening the late end.

Since lowering phi1 improved the critical 1-2 resolution at 55 C, test one more step lower from the successful 0.15/0.55 condition. This will define how far the window can be tightened before the late compound becomes too delayed, while potentially giving the strongest margin on the limiting pair.

The successful 55 C region is now bracketed, and lowering phi1 improves the critical early pair while risking a slower last peak. Testing 0.05/0.55 combines the stronger early retention benefit of low phi0 with the better 1-2 spacing seen at lower phi1, to see if a still-perfect fast method exists between injections 8, 11, and 15.

We have shown that lowering phi1 strengthens the critical 1-2 pair and raising phi1 speeds the run but hurts that pair, so 0.05/0.65 tests whether the lower phi0 can offset the resolution loss at a stronger ending composition. This is a final check for any faster-than-6.8 min perfect method at 55 C.

We have mapped the 4-minute space well; to use the remaining budget, test whether the especially favorable 0.15/0.55 window can rescue a 2-minute gradient at 55 C. This probes the absolute speed limit in the most promising narrower window for the critical 1-2 pair.

The 2-minute methods fail mainly on pair 1-2, so lower temperature to 50 C and use the favorable 0.10/0.55 window to give that pair the best chance at recovering resolution. This is a direct test of whether temperature, rather than window alone, is the key barrier to a viable 2-minute method.

With only a few injections left and many perfect methods already found, use one run to separate slope effects from window effects at high temperature by lengthening the tighter 0.20/0.55 window. This checks whether the failing high-phi0, 4-minute method can be rescued by a shallower slope, confirming that pair 1-2 is slope-sensitive rather than requiring only low phi0.

The corresponding 4-minute method at 50 C was perfect, and the 6-minute version at 55 C nearly passed, so lowering temperature one step should push the critical 1-2 pair comfortably above 1.5 in this high-phi0 window. This final comparison helps confirm temperature sensitivity of the limiting pair in an otherwise promising faster-start region.

For the last injection, target a potentially improved version of the already perfect 0.20/0.55/4/50 method by lowering phi1 one step, which should further strengthen the limiting 1-2 pair while staying close to the 10-minute threshold. This final run checks whether that window can be tightened without incurring a time penalty, refining the best-method landscape.
